title: The context window
caption: The whole chat is handed over with every message, and the space is limited: the context window.

resend.body: <keeps>The AI is handed the whole chat again</keeps>, <replies>its own replies included</replies>.

limit.body: The space for it is limited. That limit is the context window.

apps.body: <marker>Apps may manage the window their own way.</marker>

the-model-keeps-nothing.description: the Messages API is stateless: it holds no conversation between requests, and the caller passes the earlier user and assistant turns along with the new message [1].

replies-feed-back-in.description: the model's reply becomes part of the input for the next turn [1].

both-directions-count.description: the context window holds the conversation history plus the newly generated output [1].

apps-may-differ.description: the sources describe the developer API; that a chat app resends the history is an inference, and chat interfaces such as claude.ai can instead manage the window by dropping the oldest content first [1].

you-type-one-line.title: You type one line
you-type-one-line.script: You type one short line, say, find three venues in Lisbon. But what the AI receives is the whole conversation so far, from your first message to your last, and it receives all of it with every single message you send.

there-is-a-size-limit.title: There is a size limit
there-is-a-size-limit.script: That bundle has a maximum size. Picture it as a bar that fills up block by block, one block for every question and every answer, until there is no room left. That bar is the context window. That limit is the AI's attention span: how much it can hold in view at once.

the-term-to-keep.title: The term to keep
the-term-to-keep.script: The term to keep is context window. If you remember one word from today, take this one, context window.

context-engineering.title: Context engineering
context-engineering.script: There is a name for working with it: context engineering. It means giving the AI the right context at the right time, not the most context, the right one. That is what we manage today.
